AI creations could become 'new silicon species' says head of Microsoft AI | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Tech treating AI like humans is "mistaken and misguided", according to a leader in Artificial Intelligence.
 
Chief Executive of Microsoft AI Mustafa Suleyman speaks to Nick Robinson for BBC Radio 4's Today Programme, explaining why he thinks that if firms continue to develop AIs that set their own objectives, they are "essentially seeding a new silicon species which will no doubt compete with us for resources".
 
The comments are the latest in a series of stark warnings from the AI industry on the possible dangers of the technology.
 
Listen to Today on BBC Radio 4 and BBC Sounds.

How ‘Godzilla’ El Niño is unfolding across the world | BBC News
recentItems.description:
El Niño is already here. 
 
The natural weather pattern, which develops in the Pacific Ocean, is bringing extreme weather to many parts of the world. There's no clear evidence that climate change has affected El Niño events.
 
We heard from our BBC reporters across the globe about how it's already unfolding in their area.

Buckingham Palace rejects claims made in Earl Spencer book about King Charles | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Buckingham Palace has rejected claims about King Charles made by Princess Diana’s brother Earl Spencer in his new memoir.
 
The King has been accused of saying to Earl Spencer, in the wake of Diana's death in 1997, that "we'll forget her soon enough", according to excerpts published in the Daily Mail.
 
But, in a statement, the Palace said the King's "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory".

Canada could become first 'associate member' of the EU | BBC News
recentItems.description:
The president of the European Commission has backed proposals for Canada to become the EU's first "associate member".
 
Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Wednesday she wanted to work on "opening the door" for Canada, which would involve closer ties on various key sectors.
 
US President Donald Trump says that if Canada joins the EU, he'll consider cutting off trade with Europe altogether or imposing heavy tariffs.
